title: review: R3: orchestrator/merge_pressure.py — measure integration contention and defer only coupled work when the merge queue is demonstrably saturated (AP P11)
spec:
Why: nothing measures the merge queue. merge.merge (orchestrator/merge.py:25-99) fails tasks with reason rebase_conflict, daemon._stale_rebase logs stale rows with action rebase_conflict, and done-but-unmerged execute tasks wait on reviews, but no module aggregates this or informs dispatch (AP P11; brief P6).
What: new pure module orchestrator/merge_pressure.py; no daemon edits.
- assess(root=STATE, now=None, window_s=86400, cfg=None) -> {"waiting": [task ids done, unmerged, gated (pipeline.gated_at or reviews exist)], "queue_depth": len, "median_wait_s": median(now - first_green_at) over waiting or None, "recent_conflicts": count of execute tasks with reason rebase_conflict or hold_reason starting 'merge conflict' or stale rows action rebase_conflict within window_s, "recent_rebases": count of stale rows action rebased, "stale_events": stale rows with risk high in window, "invalidated": tasks whose approval was voided (events with 'approval void' or pipeline.reviews_expected reset) if detectable else 0, "pressure": none|elevated|saturated, "reason": text}. Thresholds from cfg (pool_config()['scheduler']): merge_pressure_mode = "observe"|"throttle" (default observe), merge_queue_elevated = 3, merge_queue_saturated = 5, merge_conflicts_saturated = 2. elevated when queue_depth >= elevated; saturated when queue_depth >= saturated OR (queue_depth >= elevated AND recent_conflicts >= merge_conflicts_saturated). One waiting task is never pressure.
- throttle(candidate_ids, tasks, waiting_ids, assessment, pairwise_rows=None, cfg=None) -> {"keep": [...], "deferred": {id: "merge_pressure:<waiting id>"}, "applied": bool}. Applies only when assessment pressure == saturated AND mode == throttle; defers a candidate only if interference.classify(candidate, waiting task) level is hard or soft against any waiting task; independent candidates always kept; in observe mode returns everything kept with applied False but still lists would_defer for telemetry.
- Read stale rows via schedlog.read('stale'); tasks via the tasks dir under root; tolerate malformed rows.
acceptance: tests/test_merge_pressure.py::test_single_waiting_task_is_no_pressure — one done unmerged task yields pressure none and throttle keeps every candidate

tests/test_merge_pressure.py::test_saturated_queue_defers_only_coupled_candidates — six waiting tasks, mode throttle: a candidate sharing a scope file with a waiting task is deferred with reason merge_pressure:<id>, an independent candidate is kept
tests/test_merge_pressure.py::test_conflicts_plus_elevated_queue_is_saturated — three waiting tasks and two recent rebase_conflict events yield pressure saturated with a reason naming both facts
tests/test_merge_pressure.py::test_observe_mode_records_would_defer_without_applying — saturated queue in observe mode keeps all candidates, applied is False and would_defer lists the coupled one
tests/test_merge_pressure.py::test_malformed_stale_rows_are_tolerated — a stale.jsonl with a broken line still produces an assessment
